title: Key terms; importance, problems and prospects of fruit crops production in Ethiopia
competency: Define common terms in fruit crops and list the importance, problems and prospects of fruit production in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: A perennial, edible plant grown for its true botanical fruit or products made from it.
The persistence and development of an ovary after flowering.
Farm land allocated for growing fruit crops.
Vegetative propagation from plant parts; fertilization is not involved.
Damage from long exposure to low, non-freezing temperatures; it affects tropical fruits.
The time of cool, non-freezing winter temperatures a plant needs for normal bud break the next spring.
A fruit native to Ethiopia, mostly growing wild, e.g. Agam, Kega, Shola, Koshim.

en.text: A fruit crop is a perennial, edible plant grown for its true botanical fruit or products made from it, and an orchard is land allocated for growing fruit crops. Fruit set is the persistence and development of the ovary after flowering. Asexual propagation multiplies plants without fertilization. Chilling injury is damage to tropical fruits from long exposure to low, non-freezing temperatures, while chilling requirement is the cool winter period temperate plants need for normal bud break.

screens.title: An apple tree in the lowlands
screens.ask: An apple tree is planted in a hot lowland with no cool season. In spring its buds open poorly. Why?
opts: It missed the cool winter its buds need
Its fruit was picked too early
screens.after: Temperate trees such as apple need a period of cool, non-freezing winter temperatures before their buds break normally. The book calls this the chilling requirement.

screens.why: Banana is a tropical fruit. Low, non-freezing cold causes discoloration and pitting.

screens.title: Injury or requirement?
items: Mango damaged in a cold store
Apple buds need a cool winter
Normal bud break the next spring
screens.why: Injury is harm to tropical fruit; requirement is cold that temperate plants need.
screens.clue: Is the cold helping or harming?

screens.text: A farmer in a hot lowland grows apple trees and keeps his bananas in a very cold store. Which two problems may he face?
opts: Apples miss their chilling requirement; bananas get chilling injury
Apples get chilling injury; bananas miss their chilling requirement
No problems: cold always helps fruit
screens.ans: Apples miss their chilling requirement; bananas get chilling injury
screens.why: Apple is temperate and needs winter cold for buds. Banana is tropical and is harmed by low storage temperature.
screens.clue: Which fruit needs cold, and which is hurt by it?

en.text: Fruits are an inexpensive source of energy, nutrients, minerals and vitamins, best eaten fresh. They are grown for home use and for sale, improving household food security and income, and exports earn foreign currency. Fruit production conserves natural resources, diversifies the economy and is the basis for agro-processing industries that reduce unemployment. Major fruits in Ethiopia include pineapple, passion fruit, banana, avocado, mango, citrus, mandarin, papaya, guava and grapes.

screens.ask: Activity 2.2: a family of 5 eats 2.5 kg of fruit a week. Each person eats ___ kg a week
screens.why: 2.5 kg ÷ 5 people = 0.5 kg per person per week.
screens.clue: Share the total equally among the people.

screens.ask: One person eats 0.5 kg (500 g) of fruit a week. That is about ___ g a day (nearest whole gram)
screens.why: 500 g ÷ 7 days = 71.4 g ≈ 71 g a day. WHO advises about 400 g of fruits and vegetables a day, so this family should eat more fruit.
screens.clue: Change kg to g first, then divide by the days in a week.

ideas.name: Problems and prospects of fruit production

en.text: Fruit production is new in Ethiopia: commercial production started in the late 1960s and early 1970s, most indigenous fruits are wild, and most grown fruits are recent introductions. Production is very low in the highlands, and lack of technical knowledge among small-scale producers limits productivity. The prospects are good: demand is rising, the country has diverse agro-ecologies, ample water and cheap labour, it is close to Middle East and European markets, and government policy supports the sector.

notes.text: Section 2.1 is only a glossary, so it is merged into this lesson. Its title differs: Contents says "Definition of some common terms", the body says "Key terms in fruit production".

Section 2.2 title: Contents and outcomes say "prospect", the body says "potential". p.23 "automatically profitable" is an overstatement; the lesson says profit depends on management, markets and costs.
